cleanIntro: The X-Frame book takes the Model 500 no further apart than an open cylinder — everything it publishes is done with the revolver whole. Cleaning is the bore, five charge holes, the forcing cone and the compensator if yours carries one.

steps.title: Confirm you are holding an X-Frame, not a J, K, L, N or Governor
steps.action: Check that the revolver in front of you is an X-Frame .500 S&W Magnum before you use a single step here. Smith & Wesson publishes this book only for the X-Frame revolvers, and prints separate manuals for its J, K, L and N-Frame revolvers, for the Governor, and again for the M&P BODYGUARD 38 — none of which this manual covers.
steps.prose: The X-Frame is the outsized five-shot frame built around the .500 case; a heavy N-frame Magnum reads similar across a bench and is a different gun with a different book. The model name and number are stamped inside the yoke and only readable with the cylinder swung out, so this check costs you exactly the motion the unload needs anyway.
steps.quote: There are separate manuals for S&W® (J, K, L, N-Frame, and Governor) revolvers and the M&P® BODYGUARD®38 revolver - these manuals are available free upon request or via download from our web site.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Thumbpiece forward, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Keep your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard, press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it there, then push the cylinder out to the left. Look through all five charge holes and then down the bore from the muzzle.
steps.prose: The thumbpiece has to stay held forward while the cylinder swings out — let it back early and the cylinder stop drags in its notch, which is what people misread as a seized action. Five holes is a small enough number that there is no excuse for counting four, and the bore matters too: a squib in a .500 is not something you will clear with a finger.
steps.quote: Press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder to the left (FIGURE 5).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Your Revolver, p.13

steps.title: Muzzle up, extractor rod through, count what falls
steps.action: With the cylinder held out and the barrel pointed upward in a safe direction, press the extractor rod firmly through the cylinder and catch what comes out. Count the cases against the five charge holes before you go any further.
steps.prose: Muzzle up matters on this revolver: .500 cases are long and heavy, and with the muzzle down a partly lifted case slides back into its hole where it will read as an empty chamber. One firm full stroke clears all five — short repeated jabs are what leave a case standing proud under the star.
steps.quote: With the barrel pointing upward in a safe direction, press the extractor rod through the cylinder and remove all cartridges or casings from the cylinder (FIGURE 27).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Unloading, p.27

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+ goes in this revolver
steps.action: Look at what you have been shooting and at what is going back in the box: ammunition marked +P+ must not be used in this firearm. The .500 S&W Magnum being a high-pressure cartridge in its own right does not make a +P+ headstamp acceptable in it.
steps.prose: Smith & Wesson's stated reason is that +P+ is not a defined pressure standard at all — it is a marking a loader applies to its own product, so two boxes wearing it can be a long way apart. Standard +P is permitted but the manual warns it accelerates wear and brings service forward, which on a revolver you first feel as endshake and a widening barrel/cylinder gap.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: “Plus-P-Plus” (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson® firearms. This marking on the ammunition designates that it exceeds established industry standards, but the designation does not represent defined pressure limits and therefore such ammunition may vary significantly as to the pressures generated and could be DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, +P+ paragraph, p.11

steps.title: Read the barrel marking, and fire only what it names
steps.action: Read the cartridge designation rolled on your Model 500's barrel and treat it as the only list that counts — with the alternate-ammunition table on page 11 adding 500 Special to a revolver marked 500 S&W MAGNUM, and nothing else. The manual states in capitals that cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm, and that injury or death to the shooter or bystanders may result.
steps.prose: That barrel-marking warning is printed in this book under the Model 350 moon-clip heading, but it is written about the barrel marking on any X-Frame and it is the sentence that matters when a case drops into a hole it was never meant for. A .500 charge hole is generous enough to swallow things it will not safely contain, so chambering is not permission.
steps.quote: CARTRIDGES OTHER THAN THOSE SPECIFIED ON THE BARREL MARKING MAY FIT INTO THE CHAMBERS BUT MUST NOT BE USED IN THIS FIREARM. INJURY AND/OR DEATH TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDERS AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY MAY RESULT.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, p.9 (barrel-marking warning at p.20)
steps.warn: Cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm.

steps.title: Inspect the forcing cone while the cylinder is open
steps.action: With the cylinder still swung out, look into the rear of the barrel at the forcing cone and compare it against the good and eroded examples the manual prints. Smith & Wesson asks for this before use, not only at cleaning time.
steps.prose: On a .500 the forcing cone takes the hardest gas cutting of anything in the catalog, and erosion there is the failure that opens up a barrel. What you want is a smooth even funnel; flame-cut flats and a ragged crescent at the top mean the barrel goes back to the factory for replacement, not into another cleaning cycle.
steps.quote: Before using a Smith & Wesson® revolver, you should open the cylinder and inspect the barrel forcing cone to ensure that it is in good working condition.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Forcing Cone of Smith & Wesson X-Frame Revolvers, p.14

steps.title: If yours wears the removable compensator, take it off
steps.action: Insert a 2.5mm hex wrench into the screw under the compensator, below the muzzle opening, and turn it CLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — roughly two to three turns. Then rotate the compensator a quarter turn either way with your fingers and pull it forward off the barrel.
steps.prose: This is the only part of a Model 500 that comes off anywhere in the manual, and only on guns fitted with it. The hex screw releases clockwise, which is backwards from the instinct that clockwise tightens, so a person who keeps turning it the 'loosening' way is driving the lock in harder; if the compensator will not rotate by hand the cross holes in its body take the wrench for leverage.
steps.quote: Remove the compensator from the barrel for cleaning or for a compensator change (FIGURE 34).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Removable Compensator, Removal Instructions, p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have an open, empty cylinder and, if the gun was so fitted, a compensator off the barrel. That is the whole of what Smith & Wesson publishes for the Model 500 — cylinder, yoke, hammer and lockwork all stay in the frame, and there is no further teardown to reach. Deep Clean carries the record of why for this listing.
steps.prose: The limit here is stated rather than implied: the manual forbids going past the procedure it prints, and it prints no disassembly at all.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING/DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL, OR PERFORM ANY MAINTENANCE, ADJUSTMENT, OR SERVICE NOT SPECIFIED.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.31

deepAbsentReason: The X-Frame manual documents opening and unloading the cylinder, inspecting the forcing cone, removing and refitting the removable compensator, cleaning, lubrication and storage — and publishes no disassembly of the revolver whatsoever. Its table of contents carries no field-stripping or disassembly section at all, and p.31 forbids going beyond what it prints.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHARGE HOLES
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and the five charge holes with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish each by running a dry cotton patch through to carry out residue and solvent
Work the cylinder face and the underside of the extractor star, where the heaviest .500 fouling collects
If cases have been extracting hard, clean the charge holes thoroughly with solvent before blaming the ammunition

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR (IF FITTED)
tasks: With the compensator off, clean its bore channel and ports of carbon and lead
Clean the muzzle end of the barrel it seats on, and the lock screw and notch
Check the compensator is the right one for what you shoot — one pattern is for jacketed bullets, the other for lead

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth
Remove all gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces — finger moisture left on steel starts a corrosion process
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this revolver

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION AND STORAGE
tasks: After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external, with a high quality gun oil
In a cold climate choose an oil weight that will not congeal and slow the action
For extended storage oil the bore, charge holes and internal mechanism, and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil
Do not store the revolver in leather or heavy cloth, and never with a plug in the barrel
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver

reassembly: If the compensator was removed: insert it into the front of the barrel shroud, rotate it with your fingers until the notch faces down in the 6 o'clock position, then hold it and turn the 2.5mm hex wrench COUNTERCLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — two to three turns. Do not overtighten.
Close the cylinder into the frame and confirm it locks up.
Clean the revolver again before firing if it has been in long storage.
fncheck: With all five charge holes confirmed empty and the bore clear, close the cylinder and check that it latches and that the thumbpiece releases it cleanly. Cycle the action double action and single action pointed in a safe direction and confirm the cylinder indexes and locks at every stop, with the hammer and trigger returning to the at-rest forward position. Check the forcing cone and the barrel/cylinder gap for erosion every time you clean, and if wear is noted do not use the revolver.
